title: Seasonal Shoreline Retreat on Gravel Beaches: A Two-Year Survey

headings.text: Seasonal Shoreline Retreat on Gravel Beaches: A Two-Year Survey

key_sentences: We surveyed five gravel beaches along the Eastvale coast every month between October 2024 and September 2026.
Gravel beaches protect many small coastal communities, yet they are monitored far less often than sandy shores.
Managers need to know whether retreat is steady or driven by a few events.
It describes the field method, the results for five sites and the lessons for coastal managers.
Positions were converted to distances from a fixed baseline with the short script below.
The longest retreat occurred at Long Shingle, where the beach lost 14.3 m in a single month.
Harbour Wall, protected by a masonry wall, retreated least.
Sites with a hard defence behind the beach lost material more slowly, but they also had a narrower beach to begin with.
Gravel beaches on this coast retreat in short bursts, not steadily.
The survey was carried out by volunteers from the Eastvale Beach Watch group.
